_comment_attribution: Stamps each commit with an AI-Attribution trailer via whodunit (dun), recording which agent and model produced the change and how much of the diff was theirs. Distinct from vcs.agent_author_name, which only marks that a commit came from an Orion run. auto_install fetches dun through brew or scoop; a package-managed install puts it on PATH under the name dun, which matters because the git hook resolves it by name at commit time and a missing dun silently stamps every commit undetermined.
_comment_budget: YOUR weekly budget, not your Anthropic plan's allowance. Zero means unlimited.
_comment_ci: auto_fix sends a red build back to an agent on the same branch, bounded by max_fix_attempts AND by an identical-failure check that stops sooner. require_up_to_date refuses to merge a branch whose base moved after its checks ran -- a green check is evidence about one commit, and two tickets worked in parallel can each pass alone and break the trunk together. It defaults on; stated here so it is visible rather than inherited.
_comment_gates: require_plan_before_edit is OFF for an adopted repo. In a codebase where small changes are made without writing a plan first, leaving it on means hitting a wall on the first edit, and people disable Orion entirely rather than change one setting. Turn it on when the team is ready.
_comment_limits: A limit of 0 restores the default rather than meaning unlimited: 'no limit' is never a safe reading of an absent value in a circuit breaker.

slack._comment_invite: A private channel is invisible to everyone who is not in it, and the bot is the only member of one it just created. Without these, Orion makes a channel no human can see or find. Slack user IDs (U...) or emails; emails need the users:read.email scope, which is not in the default manifest.
slack._comment_approval: A passing branch asks this channel before merging; an allowlisted reaction merges it. OFF by default, which is why the first OR-38 collect said 'waiting for you to merge' rather than asking. An EMPTY merge_approvers means nobody can approve, so require_approval without it is a gate that can never open -- they go together or not at all. A rejection beats an approval however late it arrives.

tracker._comment_agent_label: Stamped on every issue the agent files, so agent-filed work stays separable from work a person filed. The tracker equivalent of vcs.agent_author_name. A label rather than a reporter because Jira's reporter must be a real licensed account, and impersonating you would be worse than leaving it unmarked. Exported to the agent as ORION_TRACKER_LABEL.

vcs._comment_author: Commits the agent makes are authored AND committed under this alias, so git log, blame, bisect and GitHub all show orionbot rather than you. The EMAIL is what decides that: GitHub matches commits to accounts by address and ignores the name. The default noreply address carries no account id, so it resolves to nobody and displays as a plain 'orionbot' -- which also means these commits leave your contribution graph (correct: you did not write them) and will be rejected by any branch rule demanding a verified or allowlisted committer email. For a real avatar and profile, create a GitHub account for the bot and use its own ID+name@users.noreply.github.com. Putting your own address here reverts to commits appearing as yours on GitHub. Empty name disables the alias entirely.
